headline: High: Langflow’s server-side, unsandboxed flow execution can feed Plane sensitive inputs and actions, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain multiple agents; Plane accepts file uploads and issue/task content. A shared workspace or copied output could let attacker-controlled content from Plane influence Langflow prompts, but no direct automatic bridge is documented, so this is an inferred medium-risk pathway.
conditions: IF Plane content is copied or uploaded into a Langflow flow without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF Langflow nodes treat uploaded text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream agents.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any Plane text enters Langflow.
Prefix imported content with a fixed delimiter and instruction warning.
Restrict Langflow flows to trusted templates only.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent inputs.
requires-engineering: isolate shared workspaces by project.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow touches flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and stored secrets, with broad network egress; Plane stores issues, tasks, files, and notes. If Plane data is routed through Langflow, sensitive work products can be transmitted to external model providers or HTTP services by default, making leakage plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Plane issues, files, or notes are passed into Langflow flows, those contents may leave the local boundary via model-provider or HTTP calls.
IF Langflow stores per-flow credentials for a flow that also processes Plane data, secrets and content can co-reside.
mitigations: Disable external model-provider calls for flows handling Plane data.
Use a separate Langflow instance for non-sensitive content.
Remove secrets from any flow that ingests Plane exports.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on flow inputs/outputs.
requires-engineering: segregate storage for Plane-derived artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Plane is not write-capable but does accept file uploads and supports multiple instances. The pair can still conflict over shared mutable resources in a self-hosted deployment, especially if Langflow writes artifacts into directories Plane also reads or serves.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same writable directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF Langflow subprocesses generate artifacts consumed by Plane, race conditions can corrupt shared outputs.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate working directory.
Mount Plane storage read-only from Langflow.
Avoid writing Langflow artifacts into Plane-managed paths.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs.
requires-engineering: use per-agent storage namespaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is explicitly a graph-based orchestration layer that can chain multiple agents, while Plane exposes issues, tasks, and roadmaps that are often acted on operationally. If Plane content becomes Langflow input and Langflow output is then used to update Plane, errors can cascade from one system into the other without verification.
conditions: IF Plane issues or notes are fed into Langflow and the resulting output is used to create or update Plane work items, mistakes can propagate.
IF no human verification step exists between Langflow output and Plane actions, erroneous outputs can become authoritative.
mitigations: Require human approval before Plane updates.
Add a verification checklist for Langflow outputs.
Limit Langflow to draft-only generation for Plane workflows.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.
requires-engineering: log and diff all Plane mutations.

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes flow inputs/intermediate outputs; Plane stores issues, tasks, files, and notes. The profiles do not document residency or certifications, so the main compliance concern is mismatched retention or handling of the same data class across two systems, which is a plausible medium-risk gap rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF the same regulated data class is stored in both systems with different retention settings, compliance drift occurs.
IF Plane files are exported into Langflow stores, subject-rights handling may diverge.
mitigations: Classify which Plane data may enter Langflow.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Avoid storing regulated data in Langflow secrets stores.
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries.
requires-engineering: implement deletion propagation across both systems.
